headline: Ravi Menon called for common standards for AI agents that pay across borders
body: Ravi Menon, chairman of the Global Finance & Technology Network (GFTN), reiterated that Project Nexus is targeting a 2027 launch for a network that would link instant payment systems in five Southeast Asian countries and India. He drew a parallel with Project Nexus when discussing what it would take for AI agents to make payments across borders, and said the agents need interoperable standards for agent identity and authorisation.
note: Each payment system would connect to one shared gateway, and for payment firms the open question is whether agent authorisation can be standardised across borders in the same way.

evidence.text: Project Nexus is targeting a 2027 launch for a network that would link instant payment systems in five Southeast Asian countries and India.
Global Finance & Technology Network (GFTN) Chairman Ravi Menon reiterated the target at the opening of the Singapore Fintech Festival on 18 November.
Each participating payment system would connect to a shared gateway to reach the other markets on the network without setting up a separate link with each one.
He drew a parallel with Project Nexus when discussing what it would take for AI agents to make payments across borders.
Menon called for common standards to verify AI agents and check what they’re authorised to do when paying across borders.

“What Nexus is doing for payment systems, we now need to do for agentic AI: interoperable standards for agent identity and authorisation, so that an agent trusted in one jurisdiction can transact in another,”
